tone_statements.citation: Browne, Ciara. 2015. An RRG Analysis of the adjective in the Bamunka noun phrase. In: Role and Reference Grammar 2015 [International Conference on Role and Reference Grammar, Heinrich Heine University Duesseldorf], Book of Abstracts (eds. Robert D. Van Valin, Jr. & Brian Nolan, per the repository record), pp. 9-10. Open copy: York St John University RaY repository, eprint 3404 (record catalogued under Panesar 2015; the deposited file is the whole 92-page Book of Abstracts; Browne abstract = pp. 11-12). Publisher version: rrg.phil.hhu.de/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/.
tone_statements.quote: The word order of Bamunka is typically SVO. Morphological processes of verbs include tense and aspect marking using auxiliary verbs and grammatical tone (Sorsamo 2008:3). In addition to past present and future tenses further subdivisions have been identified such as Far Past (P4) and One Time Past (P5).
tone_statements.locator: Book of Abstracts p. 8, second paragraph of the Browne abstract
tone_statements.summary: Tonal Grassfields language in which grammatical tone (with auxiliaries) marks tense/aspect on the verb; statement is secondhand (after Sorsamo 2008:3) and gives no tone inventory (the held Ngeloh Takwe 2002 thesis, in rows, gives five phonemic tones H, M, L, HL, LH).

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Bamunka; this work adds none on stress. It establishes that the language is tonal (5 phonemic tones) but says nothing about stress or accent, so it cannot be cited for any stress placement.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Only tone-marking conventions (pp.7-8: H, L, LH, HL, HM, HMH, downstep; 'tone was not studied in detail'); tone of noun classes and possessive phrases discussed. No mention of stress or accent. sil.org could not be reached by automated download; copy obtained from the the Internet Archive capture of 2023-12-08.

sources.citation: Browne, Ciara. 2010. The Noun Phrase in Bamunka: Towards a Complexity Analysis. The ITB Journal 11(2), Article 4. doi:10.21427/D7VF1T
sources.note: Nothing. Brief background: Bamunka SVO, tense partly marked by grammatical tone, Grassfields Bantu languages 'exhibit highly complex tone systems'; cites 'Sorsamo, H. 2008. The Phonology of Bamunka. SIL Cameroon' for the phonology. No mention of stress. Obtained from Internet Archive copy (arrow.tudublin.ie viewcontent could not be reached by automated download to scripted download).

tone.says: Contents unknown. An unpublished taught-M.Phil dissertation on grammatical complexity in Bamunka; the article derived from it (Browne 2010 ITBJ, held and read: only a background remark that tense is partly marked by grammatical tone, phonology deferred to Sorsamo 2008) suggests at most a short secondhand summary of the tone system, not a tone analysis. The pointer's hedged description is accurate
tone.citation_as_reported: Browne, Ciara. 2010. The Bamunka Language: Towards a Complexity Analysis. M.Phil. dissertation, Trinity College Dublin. (Unpublished; attested by the author's reference list and in-text citations 'Browne 2010: 38, 39' in Browne 2015, RRG 2015 Book of Abstracts pp. 9-10; parent work of the ITB Journal 11(2) article 'The Noun Phrase in Bamunka: Towards a Complexity Analysis' that is in our rows.)

sources.citation: Ngeloh Takwe, Jeannette. 2002. Structural phonology of Bamunka. Post-graduate diploma (maîtrise) dissertation, Université de Yaoundé I, Dept. of African Languages and Linguistics (supervisor Pius Tamanji). vi+93 pp. hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7F0F-7
sources.note: Nothing. Whole work is a phonology (segments ch.2, syllable structure ch.3, tones and tonal processes ch.4, orthography ch.5). Ch.4 p.56: five phonemic tones (H, L, M, HL, LH), 'Tone in this language is phonemic'. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the 102-page scanned text; pp.40, 56, 81-82 checked on the page scan.
